author: reek
body: Equality on Text must answer the same thing whatever the branches around it are made of.

author: reek
body: The LIR selector fuses a comparison in condition position into a machine compare-and-branch. `==` on Text is a call to `__str_eq`, not a compare of the two values, so fusing it compared the two POINTERS: two equal strings at different addresses took the else arm. The tree emitter always guarded this in `is-fusable-int-comparison`; `lir-cmp-whitelisted` did not, so the bug appeared only where the LIR selector took the function.

author: reek
body: That is why the shape matters here rather than the comparison. `eq-int` and `eq-txt` compare the same two values with the same operator and differ only in what the arms return, and before the fix `eq-int` answered 0 while `eq-txt` answered "equal". Integer-typed arms made the function LIR-eligible; Text-typed arms did not.

author: reek
body: Every case below is built at runtime by `mk` rather than written as a literal, so a constant fold cannot answer for the emitter. The negative controls are what keep this honest: an implementation that always returns the else arm passes the equal cases only if the unequal ones fail with it.
